scope: Existing plugin correctness and performance follow-up; no new task, claim, runtime or implementation. Not a blocker for recovery or prepared Arc product checks.

evidence: plugins/host.ts:378-384 command rejection calls record and returns without publish.
plugins/host.ts:625-638 render diagnostic updates the immutable capped diagnostic snapshot without notifying subscribers.
plugin-integration/react.tsx:171-173 diagnostics subscribes to host.subscribe; :189 displays the captured count/list.
Activation failure differs: host.ts:174-181 records and then publishes; do not claim every error path misses notification.
findings.implication: An already mounted diagnostics consumer has no host notification for a command/render error until an unrelated publish or render occurs. No browser stale-display reproduction performed.
findings.acceptance: Use an already active plugin and a mounted diagnostics consumer; cause one command rejection and one render failure independently. Require eventual visible diagnostic update without changing plugin lifecycle. Preserve capped 100 entries, original action error, no automatic retry/provider call.

evidence: plugins/react.tsx:204 PluginView subscribes to the whole registry snapshot.
plugins/host.ts:639-673 publish rebuilds the whole registry snapshot and notifies all global listeners; slot snapshots already have separate listeners.
findings.implication: Unrelated plugin lifecycle publication can schedule mounted PluginView renders. There is no measured latency, heap growth or frame-drop result. This concerns plugin lifecycle, not every token/body update.
findings.acceptance: Before optimizing, one bounded fixture with two unrelated active plugins should measure render/commit counts during activation/deactivation of one plugin, with visible and hidden panels, while retaining renderer state and immediate revocation. If worthwhile, prefer cached per-plugin snapshots through the existing host; avoid a second registry or blanket memoization.

designConstraints: Do not fix diagnostic freshness by globally rebuilding registry and waking every panel on each diagnostic without considering targeted notification.
A diagnostic-only subscription is a candidate, not an approved implementation. Keep snapshot referential stability until data changes.
No weakening of disable/unregister/session invalidation, hidden Activity effect pausing, context authorization, or existing slot ownership.
Future owner must inspect then-current source; this review pins only these three files.

primarySource.paraphrase: A store change must notify its subscriber; React compares snapshots with Object.is, and unchanged data should retain a cached snapshot.

quality.notes: Separated observed control flow from unmeasured UI/performance implications; reused existing ownership/state authority; no speculative new framework. No implementation fixes performed.
